questions.stem: The HIGHEST CIVILIAN award of India is:
questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna (instituted 1954) is India's highest CIVILIAN honour. PVC is the highest MILITARY gallantry award. Padma awards are Vibhushan > Bhushan > Shri (second tier civilian).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The HIGHEST peacetime gallantry award is:
questions.explanation: Peacetime ladder: Ashoka Chakra > Kirti Chakra > Shaurya Chakra. Wartime: Param Vir Chakra > Maha Vir Chakra > Vir Chakra.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: JNANPITH AWARD is given for outstanding contribution in:
questions.explanation: Jnanpith (instituted 1961, first awarded 1965) — India's highest literary honour. Instituted by the Sahu Jain family (Bharatiya Jnanpith). First recipient: G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam). Author must work in any Eighth-Schedule language. in any scheduled Indian language.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Arjuna Award' in India is given for:
questions.explanation: Arjuna Award (since 1961) — for good performance OVER A PERIOD of four continuous years PLUS qualities of leadership. Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is higher (single-year stellar performance).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Consider the following about the RAMON MAGSAYSAY AWARD. 1. Instituted in 1957 in memory of the 3rd President of the Philippines. 2. Often called 'Asia's Nobel Prize'. 3. Kailash Satyarthi received this award before his 2014 Nobel Peace Prize. 4. Among Indian recipients are Vinoba Bhave (1958) and Arvind Kejriwal (2006). Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is WRONG — Kailash Satyarthi did NOT receive the Magsaysay. Instituted 1957 by the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, named after Ramon Magsaysay (Philippines' 3rd Prez who died in a plane crash). Vinoba Bhave was the first Indian recipient (1958); Kejriwal 2006 (Emergent Leadership). Other Indian recipients include Mother Teresa, Satyajit Ray, Sanjiv Chaturvedi, Bezwada Wilson.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match Indian Award → Field. A. Dronacharya. B. Dadasaheb Phalke. C. Kalidas Samman. D. Saraswati Samman. List-II: 1. Coaches in sports. 2. Cinema lifetime achievement. 3. Classical / Indian arts. 4. Literary work in Indian language (specifically modern).
questions.explanation: Dronacharya (1985 onwards) for outstanding coaches. Dadasaheb Phalke (1969 onwards) for cinema lifetime achievement. Kalidas Samman by MP Govt (1980) for classical/traditional arts. Saraswati Samman by KK Birla Foundation (1991) for a literary work in any Eighth-Schedule language published in last 10 years.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The FIRST recipient of the Bharat Ratna was NOT:
questions.explanation: First three Bharat Ratnas (1954): Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari, C. V. Raman. Nehru received Bharat Ratna in 1955 — not among the first three. Negative-stem trap.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following Indian-born figures received a NOBEL PRIZE in an Indian-citizen capacity (i.e., held Indian citizenship at the time of the award)?
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa (Nobel Peace, 1979) held Indian citizenship since 1948. Khorana (US citizen when he won Medicine 1968). Amartya Sen (Economics 1998) held Indian citizenship but worked in UK; he is the most commonly-cited 'Indian' laureate. Chandrasekhar (Physics 1983) was a US citizen. Tagore (Literature 1913) and C.V. Raman (Physics 1930) — both Indian citizens — are the other pure 'Indian-citizen' laureates.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
